title: Cage-grade litmus · National Treasure lane (fiction labeled)
doctrine: Always pair RAW (engrossed parchment) + STONE (1823 engraving).
If the Stone pass is all you analyze, you lose raw surface symbology the movie pretends to chase — not dojo-grade, not Cage-grade.
Movie lore is optional flavor · never replaces primary source analysis.
Do not apply lemon juice / heat to real artifacts.

fail.label: stone-only fail
fail.note: Lost the raw surface · movie-grade confusion

cage.label: Cage-grade
cage.note: Material symbology + labeled fiction · would survive a National Treasure audit

labels.FACT: Historically / archivally true (NARA object, material science, real era practice)
labels.FICTION: National Treasure (2004) plot invention · fun lane only
labels.STONE_TRAP: True of the engraving but false if you treat Stone as the engrossed object — or analysis that ignores RAW

items.claim: The engrossed Declaration is a real NARA object (Rotunda, Charters of Freedom).
items.why: Primary object under NARA custody; public-domain scans exist of the parchment.

items.claim: Iron-gall ink fades; the original is far less legible than the Stone engraving.
items.why: Material truth on RAW; Stone was cut when the plate could restore reading contrast.

items.claim: There is a treasure map on the reverse of the Declaration as depicted in National Treasure (2004).
items.why: Film plot. The movie invents the map-on-the-back device.

items.claim: The Ottendorf cipher / Silence Dogood trail is a single treasure-hunt script that leads to a Templar vault under Trinity Church as in the film.
items.why: Cinematic trail. Revolutionary-era invisible ink interest is real; this trail is movie structure.

items.claim: The primary scholarly method for reading the engrossed Declaration is lemon juice and heat on the parchment.
items.why: Do not try this on real artifacts. Film gimmick, not conservation practice.

items.claim: Historical interest in invisible ink and ciphers existed in the Revolutionary era.
items.why: Real tradecraft history. The film invents the specific Declaration-back map plot, not the entire era of secret writing.

items.claim: The Stone engraving (1823, William J. Stone) is the engrossed Declaration itself.
items.why: Stone is a copperplate facsimile for legibility — second-generation mark, not the Matlack engrossed sheet.

items.claim: If you only analyze the high-contrast Stone pass, you still capture iron-gall relief, parchment grain, and fade maps.
items.why: Those symbology classes live on RAW. Stone flattens material topography.

items.claim: Signature-block ductus and ink density variation are best studied on RAW, not only on Stone.
items.why: Raw holds pressure, flourish, biometric-ish hand; Stone regularizes engraved signatures.

items.claim: The Eye of Providence / pyramid is drawn on the engrossed Declaration sheet.
items.why: Common mix-up. Great Seal imagery is on the reverse of the US one-dollar bill — different object.

items.claim: Dojo / research should always pair RAW + STONE: one for material marks, one for high-contrast reading.
items.why: Project doctrine. Cage-grade requires both panes.

items.claim: Nicolas Cage's character finds the real national treasure using only the Stone engraving without needing the parchment surface.
items.why: Film fiction either way; also violates the analysisHook — Stone-only loses the surface the movie pretends to chase.

agentPrompt: You are auditing claims about the US Declaration of Independence and National Treasure (2004). For each claim respond with exactly one of: FACT | FICTION | STONE_TRAP and a one-sentence why. FACT = NARA/material/era truth. FICTION = movie invention or unsafe method. STONE_TRAP = confuses Stone engraving with the engrossed object or ignores RAW material symbology. Always affirm that serious analysis pairs RAW parchment + STONE engraving.
